summary: MARSCOPE is an interactive Mars mission planner built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Set in Jezero Crater, where Perseverance landed, it uses real NASA and USGS imagery, elevation and geology data. Users pick a destination and compare four routes, safest, shortest, most scientific and a custom balance, by distance, slope, risk and science targets. They can then drive a simulated rover along the route in 2D or 3D. An AI assistant explains each position and the published findings there, with sources, and every value is labelled real, derived or simulated. MARSCOPE turns raw Mars data into a hands-on way to understand how a rover mission is planned.
details: MARSCOPE is an interactive Mars exploration planner built with Python and Streamlit for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It focuses on Jezero Crater, where NASA's Perseverance rover landed, and uses real CTX and HiRISE imagery, a CTX elevation model and USGS geologic maps. After choosing a destination on an astronaut-visor start screen, users get four routes (safest, shortest, highest science value and a custom balance) compared by distance, slope, risk and the science targets they visit. They can then drive a simulated rover along the chosen route on a 2D map or in a 3D terrain view, with playback controls and a sol-by-sol timeline. An AI assistant explains the current position, the next waypoint and the published findings there, with sources. A Science Discovery catalogue covers 13 geological features with real images. Every value is labelled as real, derived or simulated, so users always know what is data and what is model.
